data.title: JSON
data.tagline: Represent structured data as text that programs can exchange
data.description: JSON stores objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null in a widely supported text format. APIs often use it for request and response bodies. The text must follow strict syntax, and the receiving side still needs to validate the expected fields and types.

avoid: Add comments or trailing commas where strict JSON is required
Assume parsed JSON has the correct fields
Use JSON for a large binary file
Expose secret data just because the format is readable

lessonPractice.title: An API returns {"items":[{"name":"A"}]}, but the page reads data.list and fails. What should be fixed first?

options.label: Read items from the actual JSON shape and verify each required field
options.feedback: The access path must match the received object and array levels, and required item fields still need validation.

options.label: Replace double quotes with single quotes and keep reading data.list
options.feedback: Standard JSON uses double quotes, and changing quote style would not rename the items field to list.

options.label: Catch the error, return an empty list, and stop inspecting the response
options.feedback: The crash disappears but valid data is discarded. Align the structure before choosing an empty-state fallback.

data.agentPrompt: The API returns an items array while the page reads data.list. Align the code with the actual JSON shape and validate required item fields. Show a clear failure for missing or invalid data instead of silently returning an empty list. Test valid, missing-field, and invalid JSON inputs.
